children: Labour is considering raising capital gains tax

to fund a £20bn handout for the lowest earners. The Prime Minister and Chancellor are understood to be reviewing proposals to raise CGT to as high as 45pc to increase the income tax personal allowance. The idea is laid out in a Budget submission from the Labour donor Dale Vince, warning that wealth is being “taxed more lightly than work”. – The Telegraph

The head of a mining company hoping to supply the EU with rare earths in two years’ time has said it is “paramount” to end China’s stranglehold on the supply of the raw materials used in everything from cars to wind turbines and military jets. As Donald Trump and China’s president, Xi Jinping, prepare to meet on Thursday in their second summit of the year, Rafael Moreno said it was also “imperative” that they do a deal for Beijing to ease up, once again, on its threat to ban exports of rare earths. – The Guardian

The first signs of an “autumn bounce” were seen in the housing market in September as prices increased month-on-month for the first time since May. The average price of a property coming on the market increased by 0.7 per cent, or £2,441, in September according to Rightmove, the property website. However, at £367,440 the average remained 0.8 per cent below a year earlier, and 2.3 per cent lower than the start of the summer. – The Times

Friedrich Merz, the pugnacious, stubborn German chancellor, has come out fighting in a desperate attempt to save his chancellorship. The leader who promised to transform his country’s fortunes when he took power last year suffered another bloody nose at the ballot box from the Alternative for Germany (AfD) on Sunday. The hard-Right party won state elections in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, taking 37 per cent of the vote, according to the first exit poll. – The Telegraph

The founder of Nscale, a British data centre start-up, is in line for performance-related payouts worth up to $350 million after it floats in New York. The package was disclosed in the company’s prospectus, which said it was designed to ensure Josh Payne’s “continued long-term alignment” with shareholders. – The Times
